mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The relationship is continuous and active at all levels of the rate.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust consumer demand and business investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
evidence_refs: doc:Consumer Spending and Equity Market Linkages
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average signals strong economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
evidence_refs: doc:Industrial Production and Equity Market Cycles
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is above its 6-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: doc:Payroll Growth and Equity Market Performance
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over three months signals rising inflation, prompting monetary tightening expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to higher discount rates and reduced real earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise above their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: During early-cycle expansions, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals improving labor market conditions and rising consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle expansions, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0%.
